## 0. IMPLEMENTATION CONSTITUTION

SOURCE SILENCE IS NOT PERMISSION.

MISSING DETAIL IS NOT LICENSE TO INVENT.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE IS NOT DOMAIN AUTHORITY.

MOCK IS NOT PRODUCTION ELIGIBILITY.

TEST PASS IS NOT ARCHITECTURAL CLOSURE.

RECOMMENDATION != DECISION\
AI PREPARATION != HUMAN DECISION\
CONFIDENCE != AUTHORITY\
IDENTITY != AUTHORITY\
AUTHENTICATION != AUTHORITY\
ROLE != AUTHORITY\
ADMIN ACCESS != DOMAIN AUTHORITY\
EVIDENCE != TRUTH\
EVIDENCE != AUTHORITY\
PROVENANCE != TRUTH\
PERSISTENCE != LEGITIMACY\
COMMAND != EVENT\
PROJECTION != CANONICAL STATE\
RETRY != AUTHORIZATION\
RECOVERY != AUTHORITY\
DECIDED != DOWNSTREAM AUTHORIZATION\
TECHNICAL POWER != DOMAIN AUTHORITY

Implementation proceeds:

SYSTEM → INTEGRATION → GOVERNANCE → AUTHORITY → BOUNDARIES → STATE
TRANSITIONS → DOMAIN COMPONENTS → MODULES → FUNCTIONS / INTERFACES →
PERSISTENCE → TESTS → PROOF

Inverse validation proceeds:

CODE → COMPONENT → PACKAGE → CROSS-PACKAGE INTEGRATION → GOVERNANCE →
STATE TRANSITION → SYSTEM INVARIANT → SYSTEM BEHAVIOR → ARCHITECTURAL
INTENT

A locally correct component that breaks the higher-level system is not
correct. A green unit test that violates an architectural invariant is
not PASS. A working feature that bypasses Governance is FAILURE.

## 1. TOP-DOWN INTEGRATED PROTOTYPE TARGET

The bounded integrated proof path is:

Workspace → Membership → Authority Bindings → Challenge → Session →
Question Burst → Frozen Raw Set → Post-Burst AI → Reflection → Question
Selection → Evidence → Human Decision → Governed Consequence →
CommitUnit → Audit / Event → Reconstruction

Every package must be evaluated by whether it materializes or protects a
necessary part of this integrated path. Components are not accepted
merely because they work in isolation.

## 2. GLOBAL STOP AND RECONSTRUCTION LAW

When implementation reveals an architectural contradiction:

1.  STOP.
2.  Identify the first broken architectural layer.
3.  Identify the authoritative Home-File.
4.  Identify the exact contradiction.
5.  Identify every dependent package affected.
6.  Do not patch locally.
7.  Require architectural reconstruction.
8.  Propagate the legitimate reconstruction forward.
9.  Re-run recursive validation over the affected path.
10. Resume only after the required human gate.

No coding agent may authorize its own next package or phase.

Architecture 16 defines them.

A seed, migration, admin account, first user, JWT role, environment
variable, technical root or test fixture may create development bytes.

MockProvider may be implemented. Real-provider eligibility remains
blocked until the provider/privacy/data-path eligibility chain is
legitimately closed. API key, encryption, provider marketing, model
capability, or mock success cannot close HARD-DEP-002.

## 8. NON-COLLAPSE RULES

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.
Package-specific rules in the standalone prompt add to, never replace,
these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.

adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,

prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

## 21. AI IMPACT

If AI is in scope, preserve AIOP contract, AIContextManifest,
Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

## 22. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-00 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

## 36. HUMAN GATE

Build phase: `0`. Completion does not authorize the next phase. Apply
the Architecture 15 phase gate for phase `0` when this package reaches
the relevant phase completion boundary.

## 37. NEXT ELIGIBLE PACKAGE

DAG candidate after verified completion: `PKG-01` only if its
authoritative predecessors are satisfied. Eligibility is not
authorization. `NEXT_PACKAGE_AUTHORIZED` remains `NO` until human
authorization.

structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,

package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,

but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required

attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no

## 8. NON-COLLAPSE RULES

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.

these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

## 10. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.
Specifically excluded: silent gap closure, architecture redesign,
adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

## 12. COMPONENT BREAKDOWN

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15
prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

## 13. FILE / MODULE PLAN

Follow the repository topology and file ownership constraints in
Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new
architectural layer or dependency.

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

## 21. AI IMPACT

If AI is in scope, preserve AIOP contract, AIContextManifest,
Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

## 22. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-07 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

## 36. HUMAN GATE

Build phase: `2`. Completion does not authorize the next phase. Apply
the Architecture 15 phase gate for phase `2` when this package reaches
the relevant phase completion boundary.

## 37. NEXT ELIGIBLE PACKAGE

DAG candidate after verified completion: `PKG-08` only if its
authoritative predecessors are satisfied. Eligibility is not
authorization. `NEXT_PACKAGE_AUTHORIZED` remains `NO` until human

Preserve every invariant referenced by the authoritative package prompt
and upstream Home-Files. Global non-collapse laws in this master are
mandatory. No package may weaken authority, governance, Evidence,
provenance, AI, commit, failure, recovery, security, Workspace
isolation, event, projection, retry, or audit semantics.

## 8. NON-COLLAPSE RULES

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.
Package-specific rules in the standalone prompt add to, never replace,
these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

## 10. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.
Specifically excluded: silent gap closure, architecture redesign,
adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

## 12. COMPONENT BREAKDOWN

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15
prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

## 13. FILE / MODULE PLAN

Follow the repository topology and file ownership constraints in
Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new
architectural layer or dependency.

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

## 22. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-08 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance

requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,

egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,

reconstructed. Open gaps remain open. HARD-DEP-001 and HARD-DEP-002

human review.

## 6. OUTPUT STATE

Only the package capability specified by Architecture 14 may be added.
Completion requires implementation, relevant tests, negative proof,
cross-layer validation, recursive regression, proof artifacts, and a
binary package verdict.

## 7. INVARIANTS

Preserve every invariant referenced by the authoritative package prompt
and upstream Home-Files. Global non-collapse laws in this master are
mandatory. No package may weaken authority, governance, Evidence,
provenance, AI, commit, failure, recovery, security, Workspace
isolation, event, projection, retry, or audit semantics.

## 8. NON-COLLAPSE RULES

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.
Package-specific rules in the standalone prompt add to, never replace,
these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

## 10. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.
Specifically excluded: silent gap closure, architecture redesign,
adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

## 12. COMPONENT BREAKDOWN

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15
prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

## 13. FILE / MODULE PLAN

Follow the repository topology and file ownership constraints in
Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new
architectural layer or dependency.

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

## 21. AI IMPACT

If AI is in scope, preserve AIOP contract, AIContextManifest,
Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

## 22. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-10 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

## 36. HUMAN GATE

Build phase: `4`. Completion does not authorize the next phase. Apply
the Architecture 15 phase gate for phase `4` when this package reaches
the relevant phase completion boundary.

## 37. NEXT ELIGIBLE PACKAGE

DAG candidate after verified completion: `PKG-11` only if its
authoritative predecessors are satisfied. Eligibility is not
authorization. `NEXT_PACKAGE_AUTHORIZED` remains `NO` until human
authorization.

Preserve every invariant referenced by the authoritative package prompt
and upstream Home-Files. Global non-collapse laws in this master are
mandatory. No package may weaken authority, governance, Evidence,
provenance, AI, commit, failure, recovery, security, Workspace
isolation, event, projection, retry, or audit semantics.

## 8. NON-COLLAPSE RULES

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.
Package-specific rules in the standalone prompt add to, never replace,
these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

## 10. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.
Specifically excluded: silent gap closure, architecture redesign,
adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

## 12. COMPONENT BREAKDOWN

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15
prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

## 13. FILE / MODULE PLAN

Follow the repository topology and file ownership constraints in
Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new
architectural layer or dependency.

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

## 21. AI IMPACT

If AI is in scope, preserve AIOP contract, AIContextManifest,
Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

## 22. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-16 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

## 36. HUMAN GATE

Build phase: `6`. Completion does not authorize the next phase. Apply
the Architecture 15 phase gate for phase `6` when this package reaches
the relevant phase completion boundary.

## 37. NEXT ELIGIBLE PACKAGE

DAG candidate after verified completion: `PKG-17` only if its
authoritative predecessors are satisfied. Eligibility is not
authorization. `NEXT_PACKAGE_AUTHORIZED` remains `NO` until human
authorization.

Completion requires implementation, relevant tests, negative proof,
cross-layer validation, recursive regression, proof artifacts, and a
binary package verdict.

## 7. INVARIANTS

Preserve every invariant referenced by the authoritative package prompt
and upstream Home-Files. Global non-collapse laws in this master are
mandatory. No package may weaken authority, governance, Evidence,
provenance, AI, commit, failure, recovery, security, Workspace
isolation, event, projection, retry, or audit semantics.

## 8. NON-COLLAPSE RULES

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.
Package-specific rules in the standalone prompt add to, never replace,
these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

## 10. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.
Specifically excluded: silent gap closure, architecture redesign,
adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

## 12. COMPONENT BREAKDOWN

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15
prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

## 13. FILE / MODULE PLAN

Follow the repository topology and file ownership constraints in
Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new
architectural layer or dependency.

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

## 21. AI IMPACT

If AI is in scope, preserve AIOP contract, AIContextManifest,
Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

## 22. TEST-FIRST PLAN

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-17 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

## 36. HUMAN GATE

Build phase: `6`. Completion does not authorize the next phase. Apply
the Architecture 15 phase gate for phase `6` when this package reaches
the relevant phase completion boundary.

## 37. NEXT ELIGIBLE PACKAGE

DAG candidate after verified completion: `PKG-18` only if its
authoritative predecessors are satisfied. Eligibility is not
authorization. `NEXT_PACKAGE_AUTHORIZED` remains `NO` until human
authorization.

Preserve every invariant referenced by the authoritative package prompt
and upstream Home-Files. Global non-collapse laws in this master are
mandatory. No package may weaken authority, governance, Evidence,

isolation, event, projection, retry, or audit semantics.

At minimum preserve: Identity != Authority; Authentication != Authority;
Role != Authority; Recommendation != Decision; AI Preparation != Human
Decision; Evidence != Truth; Evidence != Authority; Provenance != Truth;
Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.

these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.

adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15

domain semantics, STOP.

Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,

fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and

is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into

legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin

package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,

but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,

egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,

Command != Event; Projection != Canonical State; Retry != Authorization;
Recovery != Authority; Technical Power != Domain Authority.
Package-specific rules in the standalone prompt add to, never replace,
these rules.

## 9. GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS

Governance must remain executable inside the consequence path. Where the
package participates in a consequential operation, current Governance
State, current Authority, applicable Human Decision, Evidence
requirements, Boundary results, and commit-time revalidation remain
structural prerequisites. No documentation, UI, middleware convention,
log, mock, or admin privilege substitutes for these facts.

## 10. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

Exactly the scope stated in the Architecture 14 package manifest and the
complete Architecture 15 coding prompt below.

## 11. EXCLUDED SCOPE

Anything not authorized by the package manifest or coding prompt.
Specifically excluded: silent gap closure, architecture redesign,
adjacent package implementation, production claims from mocks, bootstrap
legitimacy from fixtures, provider eligibility from configuration, admin
bypass, allow-all boundaries, semantic TODOs used as acceptance.

## 12. COMPONENT BREAKDOWN

Use only the components, interfaces, schemas, repositories, adapters,
commands, events, boundaries, and proof harness elements required by
Architecture 14 and enumerated by the package-specific Architecture 15
prompt. If an implementation detail cannot be derived without adding
domain semantics, STOP.

## 13. FILE / MODULE PLAN

Follow the repository topology and file ownership constraints in
Architecture 14 plus the file guidance in the package-specific
Architecture 15 prompt. Folder convenience cannot create a new
architectural layer or dependency.

## 14. DATA / PERSISTENCE IMPACT

Canonical, derived, relation, operational, audit, outbox, projection,
and migration effects must remain separated according to 02, 07, 09, 10,
11, and 14. A database row or successful write is not proof of a
legitimate transition.

## 15. AUTHORITY IMPACT

No new Decision Right, HumanAuthorityBinding meaning, AuthorityResolver
fallback, Owner/Admin superpower, AI authority, or cached authority may
be invented. Any authority-bearing behavior must trace to 04 and 05 and
be current at the relevant commit boundary.

## 16. BOUNDARY IMPACT

All BND controls referenced by the package prompt are mandatory. ALLOW
is not Authority and is not Commit. DENY is terminal for the attempted
consequence. Missing required proof is fail-closed.

## 17. STATE TRANSITION IMPACT

Only transitions defined by 03 and legitimately materialized by the
package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,
Transition Authorization, and Executed State remain distinct.

## 18. FAILURE SEMANTICS

Use only `DENIED`, `FAILED_PRECOMMIT`, `COMMITTED`, `INDETERMINATE`
where applicable. Do not reinterpret `INDETERMINATE` as failure or
success. Do not infer commit from UI, logs, projections, or timeout
behavior.

## 19. RECOVERY SEMANTICS

Recovery follows 10. Recovery may restore or reconcile legitimate state
but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,
compensation, rollback, and retry remain distinct where applicable.

## 20. SECURITY / PRIVACY IMPACT

Workspace isolation, service identity, database principal separation, AI
egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,
observability separation, and admin non-authority apply according to 11
and package scope. Technical privilege never creates Domain Authority.

## 21. AI IMPACT

If AI is in scope, preserve AIOP contract, AIContextManifest,
Gateway-only path, provider adapter contract, response validation,
derived/proposal status, AI_VALIDATION_PROOF limits, BND-009, and
BND-010. No model output becomes canonical Authority-bearing state
directly. If AI is not in scope, introducing model/provider behavior is
forbidden.

Write package-relevant tests before implementation as required by
Architecture 13, 14, and the package-specific Architecture 15 prompt.
Relevant classes may include unit, contract, transition, authority,
boundary, persistence, integration, negative, adversarial, concurrency,
failure-injection, recovery, Workspace-isolation, AI-boundary, replay,
and idempotency tests. Omitted classes must be genuinely non-applicable,
not inconvenient.

## 23. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION FALSIFICATION

Before implementation, state the architectural claim the proposed
structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the
structure. If the coding agent cannot formulate this without inventing
semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-29 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.

exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

Immediate STOP on architectural contradiction, missing authoritative
semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or
inability to produce required proof.

Build phase: `11`. Completion does not authorize the next phase. Apply

semantics, required predecessor not verified, hard dependency improperly
required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority

invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,

the Architecture 15 phase gate for phase `13` when this package reaches
the relevant phase completion boundary.

without an approved deletion policy. Default is restrictive foreign-key
behavior.

package may occur. Proposal, Human Consideration, Human Decision,

but may not create legitimacy. LPVS, current Authority, reconciliation,

egress controls, data minimization, provider eligibility, secrets,

structure is intended to materialize, the forbidden consequence that
must remain impossible, and the observation that would falsify the

semantics, STOP.

## 24. POSITIVE TESTS

Prove only legitimate paths defined by the package authority. Positive
behavior must include required prerequisites and must not use privileged
fixtures as proof of legitimacy.

## 25. NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove prohibited paths remain prohibited. Negative proof is required
wherever the package can otherwise create authority leakage, boundary
bypass, cross-Workspace leakage, canonical write bypass, AI authority,
replay consequence, retry authorization, recovery authority, or stale
commit.

## 26. ADVERSARIAL TESTS

Execute all ATTACK cases mapped by Architecture 13, 15, and 16 to this
package. A known attack that is relevant but untested makes the package
`INCONCLUSIVE` or `FAIL`, never PASS by omission.

## 27. MUTATION TESTS

Execute all mapped mutations. For each mutation record: invariant
removed or weakened, expected red test, actual result, and
interpretation. If a prohibited mutation survives, classify
`TEST_DESIGN_DEFECT`; do not report PASS.

## 28. CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION

Trace the package down from its authoritative Home-Files into
implementation and back upward into the system invariant. Verify that no
local implementation choice changes domain meaning.

## 29. CROSS-PACKAGE REGRESSION

Re-run all predecessor and affected package proofs specified by
Architecture 15. Dependency-driven regression is mandatory. A previously
green package that becomes semantically invalid blocks this package.

## 30. INVERSE VALIDATION

Trace: implementation → PKG-32 capability → applicable transition →
applicable Boundary → current Authority → Governance State → system
behavior → architectural intent. Every consequential effect must
reconstruct to an authoritative source.

## 31. RECURSIVE RECONSTRUCTION CHECK

If implementation reveals a contradiction upstream: STOP, name the first
broken layer and Home-File, list dependent packages, do not patch
locally, and return for architecture reconstruction.

## 32. PROOF ARTIFACTS

Return the package-specific proof artifacts required below. Prefer
canonical-state assertions, BoundaryProof, Authority/Governance proof,
CommitUnit proof, AuditEvent, Outbox proof, migration proof,
failure-injection proof, mutation proof, cross-Workspace denial proof,
AI Gateway denial proof, diff, and architecture trace where applicable.
Logs and screenshots are not primary proof when stronger canonical proof
exists.

## 33. COMPLETION CRITERIA

Binary: required code exists; required migrations are valid; required
tests were written first; positive and negative tests pass; mapped
attacks are handled; mapped mutations are killed; affected regressions
pass; required proof artifacts exist; no forbidden shortcut exists; no
open gap was silently closed; no hard dependency was bypassed; no
upstream contradiction remains unresolved.

## 34. PACKAGE VERDICT

Only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, or `INCONCLUSIVE`, using Architecture 13
semantics.

## 35. STOP CONDITIONS

required for claimed acceptance, silent gap closure, authority
invention, transition invention, Evidence invention, Governance
invention, Recovery invention, provider-eligibility invention,
bootstrap-legitimacy invention, surviving prohibited mutation, or

When a migration is required: inspect migration head; create exactly required migration; review SQL; verify upgrade; inspect schema; verify downgrade only as schema migration behavior; re-upgrade; run constraints. Schema downgrade is not domain rollback.
